newsitem.title: USA: CVS to buy Revco in stock deal.
newsitem.headline: CVS to buy Revco in stock deal.

text.p: CVS Corp and Revco D.S. Inc said Friday they had definitively agreed for CVS to acquire Revco in a stock transaction valued at about $2.8 billion, plus the assumption of about $900 million of Revco debt.

The merger of CVS and Revco, unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, would create the largest U.S. chain drug store company based on store count, with some 4,000 locations in 24 states and the District of Columbia.

CVS is a leading drugstore chain in the Northeast and Middle Atlantic regions, while Revco has leading positions in the Midwest and Southeast. The combined company will rank second in retail drug store revenues in 1997 with about $13.0 billion, topped only by Walgreen Co.

Under terms of the merger pact, CVS will combine with Revco in an exchange of stock that is expected to qualify for treatment as a pooling of interests transaction and be tax-free to Revco shareholders.

For each share of Revco stock they hold, Revco shareholders will receive 0.4692 share of CVS common plus the number of shares of CVS determined by dividing $20 by the CVS average closing stock price. The conversion ratio cannot exceed 1.0097 or be less than 0.8837.
The CVS average closing price will be determined by randomly selecting 10 trading days out of the 20 trading days ending on the fifth trading day before the closing date.
As an example, based on Thursday's CVS closing price of $44, the bid would amount to $40.64 per Revco share.
In a statement, the companies said the deal is expected to be accretive and to yield $100 million in annual cost savings.
Following completion of the deal, CVS will implement an aggressive new-store opening program, calling for about 300 new stores or relocations per year.
